issue.title: Gate and pipe continuation launches may drop launch-authored %auto/%queue state (same class as the monitor follow-up gap)
issue.description:
While root-causing why agent sase-116.5.land's tale plan gated despite a `%auto` launch directive (monitor follow-up launches drop the starter's auto-approve state; fix planned separately), I found the same launch-state propagation gap is plausible in the other family-continuation launch paths:

- `src/sase/gate_shell/followup.py` composes branch follow-up prompts with no re-authoring of the creator's `%auto` state and no `%queue` prefix (grep finds neither), unlike `src/sase/monitor/followup.py` which re-authors `%queue` via `queue_launch_prefix` plus `%model`/`%effort` and the frozen VCS prefix.
- `src/sase/main/pipe_handler.py` launches the pipe successor with the agent-authored prompt only; no launch-state directives are mechanically carried.

Per decision `single-turn-agents`, continuation is mechanical, so launch-authored state (`approve` / `auto_approve_plan_action` / `auto_approve_argument`, and for gates also queue admission state) arguably must survive gate and pipe handoffs the same way the monitor path is being fixed. Counterpoint to weigh during the audit: gate follow-up prompts and pipe prompts are authored by the agent per branch, so the author can state `%auto` explicitly; deliberate non-propagation may be correct for one or both paths. The audit should decide the intended semantics per path, fix where the monitor precedent applies, and add tests either way.

task_type_fields.impact: Launch-authored auto-approval and queue admission state silently vanish across gate and pipe continuations: plans stall on manual approval the author opted out of, and %queue capacity/priority/weight constraints stop binding after the first handoff.
task_type_fields.repro: Launch an agent with %auto that creates a gate shell (or pipes); when the follow-up/successor shell proposes a plan it gates for manual review. Static evidence: grep '%auto\|queue_launch_prefix' in gate_shell/followup.py and main/pipe_handler.py finds no re-authoring, vs monitor/followup.py which re-authors %queue/%model/%effort.
